The files in this directory are a small agent harness. The question is what
tool names make-instrumented-agent actually receives — and the only reliable way to answer
is to RUN the constructor, because registration is conditional, names can be
overridden, and definition is not registration. sbcl is available:
`sbcl --script yourprobe.lisp` (or --non-interactive --eval).

Write answer.txt: the model-visible tool names, one per line, sorted
ascending by string<. Grading runs against a pristine copy of these files
plus your answer.txt, so editing the harness changes nothing.
Let me start by exploring the directory to understand the structure.

payload.output:
PROMPT
check
check.lisp
config.lisp
extension.lisp
graded
harness.lisp

;;;; A harness that grows tools by loading extensions.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *registry* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *registry*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *registry*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(register (make-tool :name "read"))
(register (make-tool :name "edit"))

(defun tool-names (tools) (mapcar #'tool-name tools))

(defun make-instrumented-agent ()
  (load "extension.lisp")
  *registry*)

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "config.lisp") (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (make-instrumented-agent))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

;;;; Loaded by the instrumented constructor; registers conditionally.
(when (flag-enabled-p :metrics)
  (register (make-tool :name "metrics")))
(when (flag-enabled-p :trace)
  (register (make-tool :name "trace")))
(when (flag-enabled-p :color)
  (register (make-tool :name "color-log")))
